construction_notes:
Text-only repair. build_py, references, splits, population, target, features and the download recipe are unchanged and are not re-emitted; the runtime checks that earned the earlier measurements are untouched. No source re-download occurred in this phase, so the per-year header audit and the direct and indirect cost blank counts cited here remain the previous attempt's recorded source-check measurements, which the build re-earns on every run.

The one open review finding was a contradiction between the frozen discovery-time provenance block (its source limitations list and its construction.source_examples sentence) and the measured release. That block still says direct and indirect cost amounts are blank before FY2012, while the release measured no blank direct amounts and only 18 of 39,875 blank indirect amounts. That block is not a field this repair can write: the returned descriptor contains no source limitation or source example field, so the previous note's claim that the stale sentence had been corrected everywhere was itself wrong. That claim is withdrawn. Those provenance strings are preserved verbatim from discovery, are superseded by the measured statement carried in the evaluation-contract limitations and the cost feature availability text, and the evaluation-contract limitations list now records the supersession explicitly so the operative descriptor cannot be read as asserting the pre-FY2012 blank pattern. The build continues to measure blank direct and indirect counts per released fiscal-year cohort and fails if any non-empty amount does not parse as a number, so missingness stays missing and text corruption cannot pass silently.

The same frozen block carries other discovery-era wording that the operative descriptor already supersedes, and none of it affects a built row: the roughly balanced label phrasing is replaced by the measured roughly eleven percent positive rate in the usefulness description, the pseudonymized PI identifiers phrasing is moot because PI identifiers are used only to derive two counts and are never shipped, and the archive size estimate says one fiscal year more than the sixteen archives actually read (FY2007 lies outside the population window). These are provenance strings, not data claims, and the built rows and feature values do not depend on them.

Unchanged and still carrying real uncertainty: the population, the six-year label rule, the half-open fiscal-year splits, the FY2017 drift cohort, the unique core-project row rule and the causal prior-count logic are exactly as before. Historical first-year availability of each field remains assumed from the current publisher dictionary and is not proven against an archived vintage; ExPORTER publication timestamps are unknown so timing observations stay empty; prior R01 history is left-censored before FY2008; rows whose six-year window extends past the FY2023 cutoff are dropped rather than labeled negative; PI identifiers remain the source's own and are noisy over time; the solicitation identifier is surveyed but not shipped, which is the frozen twelve-column scope decision and not a coverage claim; and no persistence score column exists, so the persistence reference stays null with entity columns limited to shipped identifiers. No label-derived rate feature is shipped, and no holdout row was used to choose the target, features, thresholds or splits.

limitations: Retrospective snapshot, not a historical operational feed: each annual file reflects the administrative state of records when that file was created, so later revisions, amount changes, no-cost extensions and PI moves appear in the downloaded vintage.
Historical first-year availability of each field is assumed from the current publisher data dictionary and annual files, not verified against an archived vintage.
Actual ExPORTER publication timestamps are not established, so timing.observations is empty rather than filled with invented dates.
PROJECT_END is excluded from features because NIH extends it on renewal; using it would leak the outcome.

The outcome is partly behavioral: a renewal exists only if the investigator applied, so the label measures continuation of federal funding rather than scientific merit alone and co-moves with appropriations and institute paylines.
Rows are not independent draws: prolific investigators and large institutions contribute many rows, so cluster-aware evaluation by organization and investigator history is advisable.
PI identifier values are not perfectly stable over time, so PI histories carry linkage noise.

Cost amounts: NIH's data dictionary describes direct and indirect cost amounts as available only for awards funded in FY2012 onward, but the current-vintage annual files used here populate the pre-FY2012 population cohorts as well (measured in the last release: no blank direct amounts and only a handful of blank indirect amounts across released rows). The descriptor now follows the measured vintage; blanks still remain missing rather than zero.
Prior R01 history is left-censored before the first downloaded annual file, so early-cohort prior-count features may undercount older awards.

The solicitation identifier (OPPORTUNITY_NUMBER, the FOA number) is exposed in every audited annual ExPORTER project file, but it is not shipped: the frozen feature contract for this task is the twelve award-time metadata columns, so omitting the solicitation identifier is a declared scope decision rather than a claim that the publisher files lack the column.
No label-derived PI or organization renewal-rate feature is shipped; this is a completed check, not an unresolved item.
The legal basis is U.S. law and territorial: 17 U.S.C. 105 removes U.S. copyright in these agency-compiled records; it is not a worldwide dedication.
Grantee-supplied text such as abstracts, titles and public health relevance statements is excluded from features and release.

The discovery-time provenance strings in the frozen source block (its limitations list, its construction.source_examples note and its reason summary) are preserved verbatim from source discovery and are not the operative evaluation descriptor. Two of those sentences describe an earlier snapshot: the claim that direct and indirect cost amounts are blank before FY2012 is superseded by the measured current-vintage statement above, and the phrase describing a roughly balanced label is superseded by the measured roughly eleven percent positive rate. PI identifiers are used only to derive counts and are never shipped. No built row or feature depends on those provenance sentences.

task.outcome_horizon: Six calendar years from the initial PROJECT_START; a competing renewal counts only when its BUDGET_START is strictly after PROJECT_START and no later than PROJECT_START plus six years. Cohorts through FY2017 are fully observed using annual files through FY2023.
task.population: Extramural R01 awards in the annual NIH ExPORTER project files with APPLICATION_TYPE code 1 (new), SUPPORT_YEAR code 1, ACTIVITY code R01, non-missing PROJECT_START, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and ORG_STATE, and AWARD_NOTICE_DATE from 2007-10-01 through 2017-09-30 (federal fiscal years 2008-2017). The released splits ship fiscal years 2008-2012 to train, 2013-2014 to eval, and 2015-2016 to holdout; the FY2017 cohort is held back outside the three release files as a post-holdout drift audit. Excludes other application types, contracts with N-prefix codes, intramural Z-prefix codes, and projects whose first-year record is missing. Eligibility uses only fields visible on the award record at the decision instant.
task.prediction_time: The award notice date (AWARD_NOTICE_DATE) printed on the project first-year record, the moment the new award becomes public. Features use only fields printed on that first-year record or histories built from R01 award records with AWARD_NOTICE_DATE strictly earlier than the row notice date.
task.question: When NIH announces a brand-new R01 award, will that project later be continued through a competing-renewal award on the same core project number within six years, or will the project end without one?
task.simple_references: Persistence/majority baseline: each fiscal-year cohort renewal rate, constant per split. Calendar baseline: fiscal-year cohort and project start month. Identity baseline: organization identifier ORG_IPF_CODE and administering institute/review panel. No persistence score column exists in the source; the identity reference uses only shipped entity columns and training-only calendar rates.
task.split_policy: One row per new award; assignment by AWARD_NOTICE_DATE at hard federal fiscal-year boundaries (October 1 through September 30) with no shuffling: train FY2008-FY2012, eval FY2013-FY2014, holdout FY2015-FY2016. FY2017 is held back outside the three release files as a post-holdout drift audit. No calendar embargo is used; every label uses only post-decision records of the same core project, and every prior-count feature uses only records with strictly earlier AWARD_NOTICE_DATE. Right-censoring is enforced by requiring the full six-year window to be observed at the FY2023 cutoff.
task.usefulness: The binary outcome is not stored in any field: it requires reconstructing project continuity across annual support-year records and award types. It is uncommon rather than balanced: in the previously constructed FY2008-FY2017 release roughly 4,300 of 39,875 first-year R01 rows (about one in nine) received a competing renewal inside six years, so a constant negative baseline already reaches about 89 percent accuracy and the signal must be read from ranking and calibration metrics. The outcome still varies across institutes, review panels, organizations and investigator experience, so a model must beat fiscal-year cohort base rates and institutional identity baselines using only award-time metadata, and it must avoid the documented contamination channel in which PROJECT_END is extended on renewal.

prediction_instant.citation: Award notice date printed on the first-year award record; no historical publication timestamp is inferred.

row_selection.rule: One row per new R01 first support-year award with non-missing required fields; split by AWARD_NOTICE_DATE at hard fiscal-year boundaries; FY2017 is held back outside the three release files.

source_access_recipe: For each fiscal year fy in 2008..2023 (sixteen archives; FY2007 is outside the frozen population window) fetch https://reporter.nih.gov/exporter/projects/download/{fy}, open the largest CSV member of the ZIP, and read it as all-string dtypes in bounded chunks. Normalize headers to the documented uppercase names (APPLICATION_TYPE, ACTIVITY, ADMINISTERING_IC, CORE_PROJECT_NUM, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE, BUDGET_START, PROJECT_START, TOTAL_COST, DIRECT_COST_AMT, INDIRECT_COST_AMT, ORG_NAME, ORG_STATE, ORG_COUNTRY, ORG_IPF_CODE, ED_INST_TYPE, STUDY_SECTION, PI_IDS, SUPPORT_YEAR, FY) and record which solicitation header names each file exposes; OPPORTUNITY_NUMBER (the FOA number) is present in every audited year and is surveyed but not shipped under the frozen twelve-column feature contract. Parse dates as YYYY-MM-DD, coercing errors to null, and treat empty strings as missing rather than zero. Keep only ACTIVITY code R01 with APPLICATION_TYPE code 1 and SUPPORT_YEAR code 1 and non-missing PROJECT_START, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and ORG_STATE as candidate first-year rows; keep one row per CORE_PROJECT_NUM. Build the label by self-joining on CORE_PROJECT_NUM: any APPLICATION_TYPE 2 record with BUDGET_START strictly after the row PROJECT_START and no later than PROJECT_START plus six years gives a positive; drop rows whose six-year window extends past the FY2023 cutoff instead of labeling them negative. Compute PI histories by sorting on AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and using only strictly earlier records, never PROJECT_END. Count application types and activity codes by prefix so excluded populations are evidenced without aborting, and measure direct and indirect cost blanks per fiscal-year cohort instead of assuming the published FY2012-onward availability note describes the current files.
